key_insight: UNSM-treated Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings showed sample-dependent hardness, with peak values of 970 HV for detonation-sprayed deposits and 1165 HV for HVOF deposits.
engineering_relevance: Selecting UNSM conditions for these coatings requires assessing local hardness alongside surface integrity, rather than assuming harder coatings resist scratching better.
method: Evaluated four UNSM-treated samples per deposition route at static loads of 20–30 N and vibration amplitudes of 20–30 µm.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN with a 10 s dwell.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings; maxima occurred at 20 N/20 µm and 30 N/30 µm, respectively.
watch_item: Post-scratch SEM observations neither isolate UNSM-induced damage nor establish a scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
